overview.heading: What is on the Wetherspoons steak club?
overview.body:
The Wetherspoons Steak Club covers individual beef steaks, gammon and mixed grills, rather than one standard steak dinner. Sirloin is described as balancing tenderness with beef flavour, while the smaller rump steak offers a firmer texture and suits a lighter appetite. Aberdeen Angus rump is the larger beef option, aimed at diners who want a more substantial steak. Those distinctions give you a useful starting point before considering the local price.

[Mixed Grill](/steak-club/mixed-grill) changes the format by combining gammon, pork loin, rump steak, lamb chop and sausage. [Large Mixed Grill](/steak-club/large-mixed-grill) expands that selection and adds fried eggs. Gammon steak provides a separate alternative to beef, with a choice of fried eggs or pineapple. Check the current menu for the complete accompaniments, which are not specified in the supplied listings.

overview.heading: Which steak club meal should I choose?
overview.body:
Choose the smaller rump steak for a lighter appetite, sirloin for its described balance of tenderness and flavour, or Aberdeen Angus rump for a larger beef portion. The important distinction is not simply steak versus grill: the individual steaks let you choose a cut, whereas the mixed grills bring several meats together. That makes the format as relevant as the size when deciding what you actually want to eat.

Large [Mixed Grill](/steak-club/mixed-grill) is the most substantial highlighted choice, with extra steak, additional sausages, gammon, pork loin, lamb and fried eggs. The standard Mixed Grill offers the multi-meat format without that expanded specification. Gammon steak takes a different route, pairing its savoury flavour with your choice of eggs or pineapple. Compare the full local descriptions before deciding, particularly if the topping or accompaniments matter more to you than the cut.

overview.heading: Does Wetherspoons steak club include a drink?
overview.body:
A drink is often included with Steak Club offers at participating pubs, but the supplied information does not identify which individual meals qualify. Tuesday is the stated day for special Steak Club pricing. Before choosing sirloin, gammon steak or either mixed grill on the strength of an offer, confirm that the meal is included and ask which drinks are eligible. Do not assume every drink on the Drinks Menu forms part of the deal.

For a useful comparison, look at the total cost of the food and the drink you actually want. A package only helps your decision if its eligible drink suits you. The smaller rump steak is the highlighted value pick, but the local Tuesday terms should decide whether it offers the best overall value for your order.

If a local menu shows a special or a changed accompaniment, compare its full description with the listed meals before ordering. Ask about its price, any included drink and relevant dietary or [allergen](/allergen-information) information rather than assuming the regular Tuesday terms apply. bestChoices.title: Best for a lighter appetite
bestChoices.text: The smaller rump steak is described specifically for a lighter appetite, with a firm texture and savoury beef flavour. Choose it when you want an individual steak rather than a larger cut or multi-meat grill.

bestChoices.title: Best for balanced steak flavour
bestChoices.text: Sirloin is the clearest choice if you want the described balance of tenderness and rich beef flavour. It offers an individual-cut alternative to Mixed Grill, without making variety of meats the main attraction.

bestChoices.title: Best for a larger beef steak
bestChoices.text: Aberdeen Angus rump suits someone whose priority is a substantial beef steak with a robust flavour. Compare it with Large Mixed Grill: the former focuses on one cut, while the latter combines several meats.

bestChoices.title: Best for variety on one plate
bestChoices.text: Mixed Grill brings together gammon, pork loin, rump steak, lamb chop and sausage. It suits diners who would rather have several meats than commit to sirloin, rump or gammon alone.
